School Life.title: Countries, Nationalities and Languages
School Life.text:
Students in an international school come from many countries.

Country → nationality → language:
Türkiye → Turkish → Turkish
Germany → German → German
Japan → Japanese → Japanese
Italy → Italian → Italian
Brazil → Brazilian → Portuguese
Egypt → Egyptian → Arabic
the USA → American → English

Language focus, the verb be (am / is / are):
I am (I'm) from Türkiye. I'm Turkish.
She is (She's) from Spain. She isn't from Mexico.
They are (They're) Japanese.
Where are you from? Is he Italian? Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.

Remember: Country, nationality and language names always start with a capital letter.
School Life.q: Hiro and Yuki ___ from Japan. They speak Japanese.
School Life.explain: Hiro and Yuki = they, so we use are.

School Life.title: Capitals and Tourist Attractions
School Life.text:
Capital cities and famous attractions:
Ankara (Türkiye): Anıtkabir
London (the UK): Big Ben, the London Eye
Paris (France): the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre
Rome (Italy): the Colosseum
Cairo (Egypt): the Pyramids of Giza (near Cairo)
Beijing (China): the Forbidden City

Language focus, there is / there are:
There is a famous tower in Paris.
There are many museums in London.
Is there a castle in your city? Yes, there is.
There aren't any beaches in Ankara.

Useful words: museum, palace, castle, tower, bridge, square, historical, modern, crowded, ancient.
School Life.q: ___ a lot of historical buildings in Istanbul.
School Life.explain: A lot of historical buildings is plural, so we use There are.

School Life.title: Activities in Capitals and Countries
School Life.text:
What can tourists do in different capitals?
visit museums, go sightseeing, take photos, try local food, go on a boat tour, buy souvenirs, watch a show, walk in the parks.

Language focus, can / can't for possibility and ability:
You can visit the Colosseum in Rome.
You can't swim in the sea in Ankara; there isn't a sea.
Can I take photos in the museum? No, you can't.
I can speak English, but I can't speak Chinese.

After can we always use the base form of the verb: She can swim (not: can swims, can to swim).
School Life.q: In London, you ___ take a ride on the London Eye.
School Life.explain: can + base verb, with no -s and no to: you can take.

School Life.title: National Days and Celebrations
School Life.text:
Every country has special days:
Türkiye: Republic Day (29 October), National Sovereignty and Children's Day (23 April).
The USA: Independence Day (4 July), Thanksgiving.
China: Chinese New Year (Spring Festival).
India: Diwali, the festival of lights.
Mexico: Day of the Dead.

What do people do?
decorate houses, wave flags, watch fireworks, wear traditional clothes, have a parade, give presents, eat special food, visit relatives.

Language focus, present simple for traditions:
People celebrate Republic Day on 29 October.
Children wear costumes.
In China, families eat dumplings at New Year.
What do you do on national days?
School Life.q: On Diwali, people in India ___ candles and lamps in their houses.
School Life.explain: Present simple with people (plural): base form, no -s. People light candles.

Classroom Life.title: Classmates and Friendship
Classroom Life.text:
Talking about friends:
best friend, classmate, deskmate, close friend, get on well with, make friends, trust, share, support, help each other.

A good friend is honest, kind, loyal, helpful and friendly.

Language focus, possessive adjectives and 's:
my, your, his, her, its, our, their
This is my best friend. Her name is Elif.
Their classroom is on the second floor.
Ali's bag is blue. (the bag of Ali)
The students' books are on the desk. (plural nouns ending in -s take only ')

Asking about friends:
Who is your best friend? What is he like? He's funny and helpful.
Classroom Life.q: Zeynep and Can are my classmates. ___ favourite lesson is Biology.
Classroom Life.explain: Zeynep and Can = they, so we use their.

Classroom Life.title: Daily and Study Routines
Classroom Life.text:
Daily routines: wake up, get up, have breakfast, catch the bus, have lessons, have lunch, do homework, revise for exams, go to bed.

Language focus, present simple:
I / you / we / they + base verb: I get up at 7.
he / she / it + verb-s/-es: She gets up at 7. He watches TV. She studies.
Negative: I don't (do not) study at night. He doesn't (does not) like maths.
Question: Do you revise every day? What time does she go to school?

Time expressions: every day, at 8 o'clock, in the morning, on Mondays, at night, at the weekend.

After doesn't we use the base form: He doesn't play (not: doesn't plays).
Classroom Life.q: My brother ___ his homework after dinner every day.
Classroom Life.explain: Present simple with he (my brother): does.

Personal Life: Physical Appearance & Per.title: Physical Appearance
Personal Life: Physical Appearance & Per.text:
Describing people:
Height: tall, short, medium height
Build: slim, thin, well-built, overweight
Hair: long, short, curly, straight, wavy, blond(e), dark, red, bald
Eyes: blue, green, brown, hazel
Other: beard, moustache, freckles, glasses

Language focus, have got / has got and be:
She has got (She's got) long curly hair.
He hasn't got a beard.
Have you got blue eyes?
He is tall and slim.

We use be for height, build and age: She is short.
We use have got for hair, eyes and features: She has got green eyes.

What does she look like? She's tall and she's got short dark hair.
Personal Life: Physical Appearance & Per.q: My teacher ___ short grey hair and glasses.
Personal Life: Physical Appearance & Per.explain: For hair and features we use have got. With he/she (my teacher) it is has got.

Personal Life: Physical Appearance & Per.title: Personality and Character
Personal Life: Physical Appearance & Per.text:
Personality adjectives:
Positive: friendly, generous, hard-working, honest, patient, polite, cheerful, confident, creative.
Negative: lazy, rude, selfish, impatient, bossy, mean, shy (not always negative).

Opposites: hard-working ↔ lazy, polite ↔ rude, generous ↔ mean (selfish), patient ↔ impatient.

Language focus, asking about personality:
What is he like? He's very friendly and generous.
(Do not confuse with: What does he like? He likes football.)

Adverbs of degree: very, really, quite, a bit
She's really creative. He's a bit shy.

We can use and / but / because:
She is clever but a bit lazy.
Personal Life: Physical Appearance & Per.q: Mert never shares his things with anyone. He is ___.
Personal Life: Physical Appearance & Per.explain: A person who never shares and thinks only of himself is selfish.

Family Life.title: Jobs and Workplaces
Family Life.text:
Jobs and where people work:
doctor, nurse → hospital
teacher → school
chef, waiter → restaurant
pilot, flight attendant → plane, airport
farmer → farm
engineer → office, factory, construction site
firefighter → fire station
mechanic → garage
software developer → office or home
shop assistant → shop

Language focus, a / an with jobs:
My father is a pilot. My aunt is an engineer. (an before vowel sounds)

What does your mother do? She's a nurse.
Where does she work? She works in a hospital.
Family Life.q: My uncle is ___ architect. He designs buildings.
Family Life.explain: Architect starts with a vowel sound, so we use an: an architect.

Family Life.title: Work Routines and Activities
Family Life.text:
Talking about work routines:
work shifts, work from home, start work, finish work, take a break, have meetings, wear a uniform, earn money, look after patients, serve customers.

Language focus, frequency adverbs with present simple:
always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never
My mother usually starts work at 8.
A nurse sometimes works at night.
My father is never late for work. (after be)

How often questions:
How often does he travel for work? Once a month.

We also use present continuous for actions happening now:
She works in a bank, but today she is working from home.
Family Life.q: A firefighter ___ a uniform at work. (always)
Family Life.explain: The frequency adverb comes before the main verb, and the verb takes -s with a firefighter (he/she): always wears.

Life in the House & Neighbourhood.title: Types of Houses, Rooms and Furniture
Life in the House & Neighbourhood.text:
Types of houses: flat (apartment), detached house, terraced house, cottage, villa.

Rooms: living room, bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, dining room, hall, balcony, garden, garage.

Furniture: sofa, armchair, bed, wardrobe, bookshelf, desk, table, chairs, carpet, fridge, cooker, washing machine.

Language focus, prepositions of place:
in, on, under, next to, between, behind, in front of, opposite
The lamp is on the desk.
The cat is under the bed.
The sofa is between the armchair and the bookshelf.
The wardrobe is next to the window.

There is a fridge in the kitchen. There are two beds in my room.
Life in the House & Neighbourhood.q: The television is ___ the two windows. One is on the left, the other is on the right.
Life in the House & Neighbourhood.explain: Something in the middle of two things is between them.

Life in the House & Neighbourhood.title: Activities in the House
Life in the House & Neighbourhood.text:
Household chores: do the washing-up, do the laundry, make the bed, tidy the room, vacuum the floor, set the table, take out the rubbish, water the plants, cook dinner.

Leisure activities at home: watch TV, read books, play board games, listen to music, chat online.

Language focus, present continuous for actions happening now:
am / is / are + verb-ing
Mum is cooking dinner in the kitchen.
My brothers are playing a video game in the living room.
I'm not watching TV; I'm doing my homework.
What are you doing? I'm tidying my room.

Spelling: make → making, sit → sitting, tidy → tidying.
Life in the House & Neighbourhood.q: Look! Dad ___ the plants in the garden.
Life in the House & Neighbourhood.explain: Look! shows the action is happening now: present continuous. Dad is watering.

Life in the City & Country.title: Local and International Food Culture
Life in the City & Country.text:
Turkish dishes: kebab, pide, mantı, lahmacun, baklava, menemen, dolma.
International dishes: pizza and pasta (Italy), sushi (Japan), tacos (Mexico), fish and chips (the UK), paella (Spain), curry (India).

Taste words: delicious, tasty, spicy, sweet, sour, salty, bitter, hot, fresh.

Language focus, like / love / enjoy / hate + verb-ing or noun:
I love eating Japanese food.
My sister doesn't like spicy food.
They enjoy cooking together.

Ordering food:
What would you like? I'd like a pizza, please.
Would you like something to drink? Yes, an orange juice, please.
(I'd like = I would like: a polite way to ask for something.)
Life in the City & Country.q: Waiter: What would you like to eat? Customer: ___
choices: I'd like the vegetable soup, please.
Life in the City & Country.explain: To order politely we say I'd like (I would like) + noun.

Life in the City & Country.title: Food Festivals in the City
Life in the City & Country.text:
Food festivals celebrate local products and cooking: Gaziantep Gastronomy Festival, Adana Kebab and Şalgam Festival, Mesir Paste Festival in Manisa, Oktoberfest in Germany, the Tomato Festival (La Tomatina) in Spain.

At a festival people taste food, watch cooking shows, listen to music, buy local products and meet chefs.

Language focus, comparatives:
short adjectives + -er: cheap → cheaper, hot → hotter, tasty → tastier
long adjectives: more + adjective: more delicious, more crowded
irregular: good → better, bad → worse
The festival this year is bigger than last year.
Street food is cheaper than restaurant food.
Adana kebab is spicier than Urfa kebab.
Life in the City & Country.q: This year's food festival is ___ than last year's. There are many more visitors.
Life in the City & Country.explain: Crowded is a long adjective, so the comparative is more crowded than.

Life in the World & Nature.title: Endangered Animals and Their Habitats
Life in the World & Nature.text:
Endangered animals are in danger of disappearing (becoming extinct).
Examples: giant panda (bamboo forests in China), polar bear (the Arctic), tiger (Asian forests), Mediterranean monk seal and loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) on the coasts of Türkiye, orangutan (rainforests of Borneo).

Habitats: rainforest, desert, ocean, mountain, grassland, wetland, the Arctic.

Why are they in danger? habitat loss, deforestation, hunting, pollution, climate change.

Language focus, present simple for facts:
Polar bears live in the Arctic.
Pandas eat bamboo.
Sea turtles lay their eggs on sandy beaches.
They don't live in hot places.
Life in the World & Nature.q: Loggerhead sea turtles ___ their eggs on sandy beaches like İztuzu in Muğla.
Life in the World & Nature.explain: Present simple for facts; the subject is plural (turtles), so we use the base form: lay.

Life in the World & Nature.title: Protecting Animals and Nature
Life in the World & Nature.text:
How can we protect endangered animals?
create national parks and protected areas, stop illegal hunting, plant trees, reduce plastic waste, recycle, keep beaches clean, support wildlife organisations, raise awareness.

Language focus, should / shouldn't and must / mustn't:
We should plant more trees.
We shouldn't leave rubbish on the beach.
You must not (mustn't) touch the turtle nests. (it is forbidden)
People must protect wild animals.

should = advice, must = strong obligation, mustn't = prohibition.
After should and must we use the base form of the verb.
Life in the World & Nature.q: Sign on the beach: Turtle nests! You ___ walk here at night.
Life in the World & Nature.explain: The sign shows a prohibition (it is not allowed), so we use mustn't.

Life in the Universe & Future.title: Films and Film Genres
Life in the Universe & Future.text:
Film genres: action, adventure, animation (cartoon), comedy, drama, fantasy, horror, science fiction (sci-fi), documentary, thriller, romance.

People in films: actor, actress, director, character, hero, villain.

Adjectives: exciting, boring, funny, scary, thrilling, amazing, moving, realistic.

Language focus, past simple to talk about films you watched:
regular verbs + -ed: watch → watched, enjoy → enjoyed
irregular verbs: see → saw, go → went, be → was / were
I watched a sci-fi film last night. It was amazing.
We didn't like the ending.
Did you see the new animation film? Yes, I did.
Life in the Universe & Future.q: Last weekend we ___ to the cinema and watched a comedy.
Life in the Universe & Future.explain: Last weekend shows the past: past simple of go is went.

Life in the Universe & Future.title: Futuristic Films, Ideas and Technology
Life in the Universe & Future.text:
Science fiction films show ideas about the future: robots, time travel, flying cars, space colonies, artificial intelligence, holograms, virtual reality, teleportation.

Some old sci-fi ideas are real today: video calls, smart watches, self-driving cars, voice assistants.

Language focus, will for predictions about the future:
will + base verb
In the future, robots will do the housework.
People will travel to Mars.
We won't (will not) use paper money.
Will cars fly? I think they will.

I think / I don't think / Maybe / Probably:
Maybe we will live on the Moon.
I don't think people will stop reading books.
Life in the Universe & Future.q: I think people ___ holiday in space in fifty years.
Life in the Universe & Future.explain: A prediction about the future: will + base verb. People will go on holiday.
